summary: Session 1 shipped ai_router/verify_type.py: the operator's three-branch rule as one entry point (project-verify-type.txt at the project root, else the machine default confirmed once and written there, else guided setup in the terminal), and made config.load_config DERIVE transport.profile from it instead of defaulting it independently. Where a project has committed an answer, that answer IS the profile -- over the tracked config and over a seat-local local-overrides.yaml both -- so the two facts cannot disagree; the api default survives as the last step of resolution rather than as a parallel answer beside it. An unconfirmed environment default never silently re-routes dispatch, and a resolution names a transport profile only when the project has committed one. Five verification rounds settled the precedence rule: the first anchor that lands in a project answers outright, the loaded config's project before the caller's, and a project that has committed nothing is answered by its own configured profile rather than by another project's file. 16 falsifiers (both directions, look-alikes, and a structural bijection against config's profile vocabulary); full pytest 3952 passed / 9 skipped.

reason.specifics: Session 2 (the qualified verdict) reasons about the precondition this session just defined -- that a resolution names a transport profile only when the project has committed one -- and touches verification*.py / session_state.py with that guarantee in hand.
